text:
**Short answer:** The **JBL Charge 6** is the most consistently recommended pick for pool and beach use. For a big-sound pool party, the **JBL Boombox 4** is the top pick from RTINGS.

## Top pick: JBL Charge 6
- **Why:** Three of the sources name it their top overall waterproof pick. It's rated IP68, has about 20 hours of battery (28 with Playtime Boost), and doubles as a power bank. [What Hi-Fi](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart) lists it at $129.99 at Walmart and $149.95 at Amazon. [Tom's Guide](https://www.tomsguide.com/best-picks/best-waterproof-speakers) and [iTechGuides](https://www.itechguides.com/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers-for-the-beach-pool-and-shower/) also recommend it.
- **Buy:** Compare prices on the [What Hi-Fi roundup](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart), which links to retailers. I don't have a direct store link for it.

## Other strong options
- **JBL Boombox 4 (biggest, longest battery):** RTINGS' top pick. It floats, has over 40 hours of battery, and is loud, but it's large and heavier. [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth)
- **Ultimate Ears EPICBOOM (360° sound):** RTINGS' mid-range pick. It floats and has a 360-degree design, with about 15 hours of battery. Tom's Guide names it best overall, rated IP67. [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth), [Tom's Guide](https://www.tomsguide.com/best-picks/best-waterproof-speakers)
- **JBL Grip (best for portability):** About 0.85 lb, can-shaped, IP68, 12 hours of battery, $100. Its mesh gets dusty. [Good Housekeeping](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/what-to-buy/a71783745/best-waterproof-speakers/)
- **Ultimate Ears WONDERBOOM 4 (budget):** IP67, floats, up to 14 hours of battery. Tom's Guide lists it at $65 on sale. [Tom's Guide](https://www.tomsguide.com/best-picks/best-waterproof-speakers)
- **Soundcore Boom 2 Plus (loud, floats):** 100 W, IPX7, up to 20 hours at half volume, and it can charge a phone. It's heavy at 3.8 kg. The listing shows $249.99 with code AFSC20 for $200 at checkout (expires 2026-12-31). The code was tested on 2026-10-22, but confirm it at checkout. This is an affiliate page, so the seller earns a commission. [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/soundcore-boom-2-plus) · [Buy at Soundcore](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-boom-2-plus)
- **Soundcore Boom 2 (base model):** Tom's Guide notes it has no dust rating, so keep it on a towel at the beach. [Tom's Guide](https://www.tomsguide.com/best-picks/best-waterproof-speakers)

## Before you buy
- **IP ratings don't cover salt or chlorine.** RTINGS notes they only test water ingress, and recommends rinsing with fresh water after use. [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth)
- **For beaches, look for dust protection too.** Good Housekeeping suggests IP5X or IP6X for sand. [Good Housekeeping](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/what-to-buy/a71783745/best-waterproof-speakers/)
- **Keep ports closed and dry them before charging.** Put the speaker on a towel, not in sand. [iTechGuides](https://www.itechguides.com/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers-for-the-beach-pool-and-shower/)

**My suggestion:** Get the JBL Charge 6 for the best balance of sound, durability, and battery. Choose the Boombox 4 if you want the loudest party speaker and don't mind the weight. Choose the JBL Grip or Wonderboom 4 if you mostly want something light to carry.
